issue.title: Who gets the £100 energy payment: every home in bands A to D, or those in need?
issue.question: The £100 energy payment goes to homes in council tax bands A to D in England. Should it go to every home in those bands, or be aimed at the households who struggle most?
issue.summary: On 24 November 2026 the government set out a £100 Household Energy Payment for up to 20 million households in England in council tax bands A to D. About 13 million are due to be paid automatically, councils start paying on 4 January, and the scheme stays open until the end of May. A separate £100 million fund lets councils help vulnerable households outside the main scheme and set their own rules for it (s1). Homes in bands E to H are left out of the main payment, so some low-income households miss out while some better-off homes in bands A to D are paid (s2). Cornwall Insight forecasts that the January price cap will rise 26%, from £1,723 to £2,166 for a typical household. That is not an official figure, and Ofgem was due to announce the real one on 25 November (s3).
issue.slot_reason: The first energy issue, on 17 November, predicted that Ofgem's January price cap would top £2,000 a year, and that check falls due on 30 November. Today, 25 November, is the day Ofgem is due to announce the cap, and yesterday the government published the rules for the £100 payment meant to soften the rise.

news.headline: Government sets out £100 Household Energy Payment for up to 20 million English households, paid from 4 January

poll.finding: 70% feel they need more state support on energy bills this winter, and 66% say the Government has not gone far enough to tackle energy bills.
